summary: The rank computation in percentile.py does not follow DESIGN-001. It uses int(p*N/100), which is floor, as the 0-based index. The design requires ceil(p*N/100)-1 in integer arithmetic. The result is off by one whenever p*N is a multiple of 100, so the code violates the contract, and by hand-tracing at least TEST-010, TEST-011 and TEST-012 would fail. The tests themselves are faithful and meaningful. I could not run pytest because the command was denied, so this finding comes from tracing the code.

checklist.item: Code matches design contract (signature, errors, boundaries)
checklist.note: Signature and ValueError checks match. The rank formula does not: floor instead of ceil-1, and float division instead of integer arithmetic.
Only the requested function is implemented.

checklist.item: Each unit TEST spec implemented with TEST_nnn token
checklist.note: TEST-001..012 all present and faithful to the procedure and expected values.
Concrete expected values, no skips and no swallowed exceptions. The tests are correct and would detect this defect.

checklist.item: Obvious defects, unsafe or dead code
checklist.note: Rank off-by-one, see F-1. The min(..., count-1) clamp only masks p=100.

findings.description: percentile.py line 20 uses index = min(int(p*count/100), count-1). It is floor, not ceil(p*N/100)-1, and uses float division. For p*N a multiple of 100 it returns the next element. N=5,p=40 gives 35 instead of 20 (TEST-010 and AC-001-3). N=100,p=29 gives 30 instead of 29 (TEST-011). N=5,p=80 gives 9 instead of 5 (TEST-012). N=5,p=100 only works because of the clamp. The design prescribes index = -(-p*N // 100) - 1 with integer arithmetic. Fix the code. Do not change the tests.
